summary: Defines a basic set of SNMP managed objects for the events that can be generated by PacketCable and IPCablecom compliant Multimedia Terminal Adapter devices. This is a Proposed Standard, later updated by RFC 9141.

eli5.summary: Cable-phone adapter boxes can report things that happen to them. This memo makes a standard list of what they can report to the people running the network.

questions: snmp events for cable voice adapters
what is the packetcable event mib
how do mtas report events over snmp and syslog
what is an event class in the event mib
how does event throttling work in snmp
subtitle: An SNMP MIB for choosing how cable voice adapters log, send and throttle their management events.

tldr.problem: PacketCable and IPCablecom Multimedia Terminal Adapters (MTAs) must generate management events, and operators need a standard way to control where those events go and how often.
tldr.mechanism: The PKTC-IETF-EVENT-MIB module defines SNMP objects to configure syslog delivery, group events into classes, throttle transmissions, list the events a device can generate and keep a log of those that occurred.
tldr.outcome: It defines no events itself, only the mechanism to manage them. It is a Proposed Standard, later updated by RFC 9141.

today: RFC 5428 is a Proposed Standard that has not been obsoleted, but it was later updated by RFC 9141, so check that RFC for changes to the MIB module.

sections.title: Events on Cable Telephony Adapters
sections.content:
A Multimedia Terminal Adapter (MTA) delivers broadband Internet, data and/or voice together with telephony service to a customer's premises over a cable network. It is provisioned by the cable company (the multiple system operator, or MSO) and has endpoints, which are the telephone ports.

MTAs compliant with PacketCable, ETSI or ITU-T IPCablecom are required to generate management events when certain operational conditions occur, for instance an AC power failure with the MTA running on battery. Vendors may also define their own events. The full list of conditions is in other specifications, and this RFC does not define any events.

When an event happens, it can be stored in a local log, or sent by SNMP or syslog, and the choice must be configurable by a management station for each event. This MIB module is the way to do that. It is meant to update the event MIBs from which it is partly derived: the PacketCable 1.5 Management Event MIB Specification and the ITU-T IPCablecom management event mechanism MIB requirements.
sections.eli5: A phone adapter box notices things, like the power going out. This memo is the control panel that decides whether it writes the news down, tells a server, or both.

sections.title: Structure of the MIB
sections.content:
The module is identified as pktcIetfEventMib and registered as { mib-2 182 }. It is written in SMIv2 and imports from several other MIB modules, including SNMPv2-SMI, IF-MIB, INET-ADDRESS-MIB, SNMP-TARGET-MIB, SNMP-NOTIFICATION-MIB and SYSLOG-TC-MIB. A device implementing it is also assumed to implement the interfaces group of IF-MIB.

The object tree is split into sub-trees:

  • pktcEventControl: controls event generation (reset, syslog settings, event classes).
  • pktcEventThrottle: limits how fast events are sent by syslog or SNMP.
  • pktcEventStatus: reports the status of event transmissions.
  • pktcEvents: lists every event the device can generate, with descriptions.
  • pktcEventLog: stores the events that were generated.
  • pktcEventNotifications: defines the SNMP trap and inform messages. SNMPv1 traps are disallowed.
sections.eli5: The MIB is a filing cabinet with labelled drawers: one for settings, one for slow-down rules, one for status, one for the list of possible events, and one for the diary of what happened.

sections.title: Controlling Reporting, Classes and Throttling
sections.content:
Each event has a pktcEventReporting setting with four bits: local (local log), syslog, snmpTrap and snmpInform. When nothing else is specified, events of severity emerg, alert, crit or err default to local, syslog and snmpInform. Other events default to local and syslog.

For syslog delivery, the MIB lets a manager set the server address, port, message format (BSD syslog or the newer syslog protocol) and transport (UDP, TLS or BEEP). The device lists what it supports in pktcEventSyslogCapabilities. The default transport is TLS and the default port is 6514. A DNS-name address type is disallowed, because an unresolvable name would leave the device with no syslog server.

Event classes group events so a manager can enable or disable them together, or filter them by severity. The device MUST create one class, index 100, named generic, which holds every event not in another class. If an event is in several classes, the lowest index wins.

Throttling limits transmissions, not local logging. The admin status can be unconstrained, maintainBelowThreshold, stopAtThreshold or inhibited. The threshold is a count of events per interval; the defaults are 2 events per interval of 1 second. An event that triggers both SNMP and syslog counts as one event.

Finally, pktcEventReset lets a manager clear the event log, reset event descriptions to factory defaults, or both. It always reads back as 00.
sections.eli5: For each kind of event you can choose: write it in the diary, shout it to a server, or both. You can also tell the box to stop shouting if it is shouting too often.

sections.title: The Event Table and the Event Log
sections.content:
The pktcEventTable is indexed by an organization number and an event identifier. The organization is the IANA private enterprise number of whoever defines the event (the RFC gives 4491 for CableLabs), and the identifier is unique within that organization. Each entry holds a syslog facility, a severity level, the reporting bits, a human-readable text (up to 127 characters) and an event class. For PacketCable, IPCablecom or ETSI events the facility MUST be local0(16). Entries persist across resets and reboots.

The pktcEventLogTable records events that actually happened, in order of an index. Each entry copies the event's details at the time it occurred: a timestamp, organization, identifier, text, the endpoint name, which actions were taken, the targets used, a correlation ID from the last provisioning flow, and vendor-specific additional information. Entries cannot be deleted one by one, only cleared through the reset object, and the table need not survive a reset. When the index reaches 2^32-1, or a device without non-volatile storage resets, new events start again at index 1.

The single notification, pktcEventNotification, carries the log time, organization, identifier, endpoint name, correlation ID and the MTA's MAC address.
sections.eli5: One list says every thing that could possibly happen. A second list, the diary, notes what really did happen, and when.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Many objects are read-write, and changing them without protection can hurt network operations. The RFC lists the threats as errors going unreported, events being redirected, or reporting being reduced, which can hide misconfiguration and denial-of-service attacks that event reporting would otherwise catch.

pktcEventReset gets special mention. A rogue manager could reset the event table so another manager no longer sees its modified descriptions, or clear local logs. The module does not address contention between several managers, and says to use the reset object with caution. Reading the log table and the transmission status may also reveal sensitive information.

The RFC recommends SNMPv3 with its cryptographic authentication and privacy, and says deploying SNMP versions earlier than SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED. It is the operator's job to give access only to principals with legitimate rights.
sections.eli5: If anyone could change the settings, they could make the box stay quiet about trouble. So only trusted people should be allowed to touch them.

items.label: unconstrained
items.desc: Send event messages regardless of the threshold.

items.label: maintainBelowThreshold
items.desc: Suppress messages that would exceed the threshold in the interval.

items.label: stopAtThreshold
items.desc: Stop sending once the threshold is reached, until a manager changes the setting or the device resets.
